newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said South Africa had accessed the Lome convention. He said the membership would cover political and institutional matters while trade and development were treated separately.
Vale de Almaida said that at the ACP/EU Council on Thursday the EU had received full support from the ACP countries on the banana regime currently discussed by a World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel.
Vale de Alemaida said the EU and the ACP representatives had made a joint declaration on Zaire following the UN Secretary General Kofi Annan'a call on access for humanitarian aid.
Spokeswoman Sophie Petzell briefed on Monday's Justice and Home Affairs Council. She said the High Level Group's report on organised crime would be the only point on the agenda.

Spokesman Gerry Kiely said the Cereals Managment Committeee had decided an export levy on cereals. He said this measure was to compensate the recent cereal price increase. Kiely answered criticisms by saying that the Common Agricultural Policy's stabilizing role was to prevent prices from falling but also from rising.
On the EU/U.S. veterinary negotiations, Kiely said the Commission had called its negotiators back because no progress had been made and because their room for manoeuvre was exhausted.

In answer to a question Kiely said that Commissioner Franz Fischler considered the administrative measure to block EU meat into the U.S., announced to take place on April 30, was illegal, disproportionate and contradictory. He said the U.S. had problems meeting the EU veterinary standards and not the opposite. Kiely said that if these measures entered into force the EU would bring them to the WTO. He added that there were no indications that the date or decision was going to change.
Spokesman Patrick Child said there were no provision foreseen in the EU Treaty allowing countries that had entered the EMU to leave subsequently.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/349: Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro wlcomes South Africa's accession to the Lome convention: an historical event.
- IP/97/350: New Computerised Transit System - the Commission organises a conference in Brussels on April 28, 1997.
- IP/97/351: ELECTRABEL: The Commission obtains satisfaction on the revision of the statutes of mixed intercommunal electricity distribution companies in Belgium.
- IP/97/352: Commission clears franchise of UK privatised Thameslink Railway Network.

- IP/97/353: The Commissione refers the case Rheinmetall / British Aerospace / STN to the Bundeskartellamt as far as the affected markets for systems leadership for armoured vehicles are concerned and otherwise clears the planned concentration.
- IP/97/354: Commission proposes reduced anti-dumping duties on cotton.
- IP/97/355: "EUR" - the new currency code for the euro.
- IP/97/356: Kyrgyzstan: Commission approves humanitarian aid worth ECU 2.15 million.
- IP/97/357: Commission clears Liner Shipping Consortia.
- Memo/97/47: Calendar of the Commissioners activities for the week from April 28 to May 4.
- ME97/25.4: Midday Express.
